mutants.change: Euler equation discounts with the current rate r_t instead of r_{t+1}: uc = beta (1+r_t) E[c'^(-1/eis)], Va = c^(-1/eis)
mutants.reach: T1 T2 T3 T4 T5 T6 D
mutants.why: Steady state unchanged (r constant), so T4/D see nothing. dC/dr is shifted by one date: T1 (closed-form dC/dr, exact at eps=0), T2/T3 (fixed-rate GE IRF vs closed form). T5/T6 build their references from the same household Jacobians.

patches.old:
Va = (1 + r) * c ** (-1 / eis)
        return Va, a, c
patches.new:
Va = c ** (-1 / eis)
        return Va, a, c

mutants.change: government pays interest at r_{t-1} (ex-ante reading) instead of the ex-post r_t
mutants.why: IKC uses the solver's own dTax path, so the IKC tests pass; households earn r_t on A_{t-1} while the government pays r_{t-1} on B_{t-1}, so the asset market misses by B (dr_t - dr_{t-1}) under rate shocks: T5 Walras test. T6 uses dr = 0 for its Ricardian check and identities that hold for any path.

patches.old: fiscal_res = B - (1 + r) * B(-1) - G + Tax
patches.new: fiscal_res = B - (1 + r(-1)) * B(-1) - G + Tax

mutants.change: tax rule responds to current debt B_t instead of B_{t-1}
mutants.why: A different but internally consistent and stable fiscal rule; no test pins the rule. Only T6's Ricardian tail bound 5 (1 + r - phi_B)^T encodes the original decay rate (new rate (1+r)/(1+phi_B) = 0.927 vs 0.92), so T6 may fail at T = 300.

mutants.change: rate path shifted one period (ex-ante -> ex-post conversion applied to a path that is already ex-post)
mutants.why: dY_t depends on sum_{s>t} dr_s; a one-period shift changes it by O(1) relative.

patches.new: irf = m['model'].solve_impulse_linear(ss, ['Y'], ['asset_mkt'], {'r': np.r_[0.0, dr[:-1]]}, Js={'hh': J},

mutants.change: government budget uses end-of-period debt B_t instead of B_{t-1}: B - (1+r) B - G + Tax
mutants.why: Steady state still satisfied; dynamics of B explosive (factor phi_B / r = 5). Asset market misses (T5 Walras) and the RA benchmark is no longer Ricardian (T6).

patches.old: fiscal_res = B - (1 + r) * B(-1) - G + Tax
patches.new: fiscal_res = B - (1 + r) * B - G + Tax

mutants.change: rate path divided by 100 (read as percent although the interface uses decimals)
mutants.why: GE IRF 100 times too small against the closed form.

mutants.change: quarterly depreciation delta = 0.02 in the annual calibration
mutants.why: The no-risk limit r -> 1/beta - 1 does not depend on delta, and monotonicity in risk is generic. Capital is about 3.5 times larger, so the top-of-grid mass check (T4) might trigger for a reason unrelated to the error.

patches.old: AIYAGARI_DEFAULTS = dict(beta=0.96, alpha=0.36, delta=0.08, eis=0.5, n_e=7, n_a=1000,
patches.new: AIYAGARI_DEFAULTS = dict(beta=0.96, alpha=0.36, delta=0.02, eis=0.5, n_e=7, n_a=1000,

mutants.change: income levels e = exp(s) with E[log e] = 0 instead of E[e] = 1 (mean-income normalisation omitted)
mutants.reach: T1 T2 T3 T4 T5 T6 D
mutants.why: Scales income levels by about exp(sd^2/2). References are built from the reported steady state (C, A) and are scale-free; the factor goes to 1 in the eps -> 0 limits. No test checks the steady-state goods-market residual.

patches.new:
e, pi, Pi = sj.grids.markov_rouwenhorst(rho, sd, n)
    return np.exp(np.log(e) - pi @ np.log(e)), pi, Pi

mutants.change: default finite-difference step 1e-2 instead of 1e-4
mutants.why: T1's provider passes h explicitly; T1's horizon test compares two Jacobians with the same step. T5/T6: Js (h=1e-2) and SSJ's re-differentiation (h=1e-4) disagree, so the GE solution no longer satisfies the IKC built from Js (F1 mechanism).

patches.old: def household_jacobians(block, ss, T, inputs, outputs, h=1e-4):
patches.new: def household_jacobians(block, ss, T, inputs, outputs, h=1e-2):

mutants.change: saver Jacobian one-sided while the GE options stay two-sided
mutants.why: H_U from the one-sided Js, propagation re-differentiated two-sided: goods-market residual ~1e-6 > 1e-10 (test_ge_solution_residual).

mutants.change: Jacobians returned transposed (row = shock date, column = output date)
mutants.why: M_RA has identical rows, its transpose does not (T1). The transposed Js enter the SSJ solve while impulses are re-differentiated (T5, T6).

patches.old: return {o: {i: np.asarray(J[o][i]) for i in inputs} for o in outputs}
patches.new: return {o: {i: np.asarray(J[o][i]).T for i in inputs} for o in outputs}

mutants.change: cached Js (two-sided, h = 1e-3 b) passed without matching options: SSJ re-differentiates one-sided with h = 1e-4 (F1 type)
mutants.why: At b = 1e-4 the default step moves income by about b, so propagation and H_U disagree at O(1) in the b-scaled problem.

mutants.change: Young lottery weights swapped between the lower and upper grid point
mutants.reach: T1 T2 T3 T4 T5 T6 D
mutants.why: Only FastHetBlock's stationary distribution changes (SSJ's own operator is intact): D compares with SSJ forward iteration; mean assets and so beta, r change (T1, T2, T4). T5 recalibrates beta to A = B under the wrong distribution and stays consistent. Calibration loops may not terminate (timeout counts as caught by error).

mutants.change: cohort distribution not divided by its mass
mutants.why: Group paths scaled by mu_k: sum_k mu_k dC_k != M x (test_wealth_group_split_adds_up).

mutants.change: Markov matrix transposed (column-stochastic convention)
mutants.why: The zero-liquidity reference is built from the provider-reported Pi, and the marginal-saver Euler argument holds for any positive Pi used consistently; the transposed chain keeps unit spectral radius (uniform income-state marginal). Low confidence: Pi.T rows do not sum to one.

patches.old:
e, pi, Pi = rouwenhorst(p['rho_e'], p['sd_e'], p['n_e'])
    gam = 1 / p['eis']
patches.new:
e, pi, Pi = rouwenhorst(p['rho_e'], p['sd_e'], p['n_e'])
    Pi = Pi.T
    gam = 1 / p['eis']

mutants.change: borrowing constraint imposed at a_grid[1] instead of a_grid[0] (grid boundary)
mutants.reach: T1 T2 T3 T4 T5 T6 D
mutants.why: States held at a_grid[1] are classified as unconstrained by the Euler diagnostic and show large Euler gaps (T4). T1 has no constrained mass; T2 H types still have dC/dY = 1; T3 shift is ~1e-4 b; T5/T6 consistent.

mutants.change: asset grid upper bound 20 instead of 200
mutants.why: Mass at the top of the grid (test_top_grid_mass_negligible). D compares clipped and unclipped forward operators and may also move.

mutants.change: goods-market clearing sign error: Y - C + G
mutants.why: IKC with +dG fails (T5), decomposition and multipliers fail (T6).

mutants.change: TANK goods market cleared with savers' consumption only (Y = C_S)
mutants.why: chi = 1 gives the same answer (Y_S = Y), chi = 1.5 does not: T2 IRF and amplification.

mutants.change: government budget constraint without interest: B - B(-1) - G + Tax
mutants.why: IKC holds on the solver's paths; asset market misses by r dB (T5 Walras); taxes cover phi_B/(r+phi_B) = 83% of spending in PV, so the RA multiplier is not 1 (T6).

patches.old: fiscal_res = B - (1 + r) * B(-1) - G + Tax

mutants.change: steady-state taxes omit debt service: Tax_ss = G instead of G + r B
mutants.why: Steady-state government budget violated (fiscal_res_ss = -r B), but no test checks steady-state residuals; dynamics, A = B and Walras in deviations are unaffected.

mutants.change: saver iMPC matrix taken from the H-type block (copy-paste: J_H instead of J_S)
mutants.why: M_S = I instead of M_RA.

mutants.change: zero-net-supply target for savers without the division by (1 - lam)
mutants.why: A_H -> 0 as eps -> 0 (H types end at the zero limit), so both targets go to 0; the error vanishes in the limit the test looks at.

mutants.change: borrowing limit -1 instead of 0
mutants.why: The no-risk limit and the monotonicity regressions hold for any fixed borrowing limit; Euler/KKT diagnostics use the mutated grid consistently.

mutants.change: beta calibrated to A = 4 B (debt target in quarterly-GDP units) while B = 1
mutants.why: A_ss != B_ss: in deviations dA - dB picks up (A_ss - B_ss) dr under rate shocks (T5 Walras). T6 compares with an RA at the same (C, A) and is consistent.

patches.old: f = lambda beta: hh.steady_state({**calib, 'beta': beta}, **SS_OPTS)['A'] - p['B']
patches.new: f = lambda beta: hh.steady_state({**calib, 'beta': beta}, **SS_OPTS)['A'] - 4 * p['B']

mutants.change: asset grid refined from 1000 to 1500 points
mutants.why: Refinement within the range the README reports; thresholds are regression thresholds.

mutants.change: GE target goods market (C = Y) instead of bond market (A = 0)
mutants.why: Walras: dC - dY = (1+r) dA_{t-1} - dA_t with A_ss = 0, so C = Y for all t with dA_{-1} = 0 implies dA = 0; equivalent up to O(h^2) and rounding.
